newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-JAPANESE REFUSE TO RESCHEDULE DOWNHILLS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-JAPANESE REFUSE TO RESCHEDULE DOWNHILLS.

text.p: Japanese organisers of two World Cup women's downhill races were accused of inflexibility on Thursday by international ski officials after they refused to hold two races on Friday to avoid worsening weather.

International Ski Federation (FIS) officials favoured adding a second race on Friday on the downhill course for next year's Nagano Olympics instead of jeopardising the second race's scheduled Saturday start.

Japanese organisers agreed to hold Friday's race an hour earlier, but refused to advance the Saturday downhill to avoid disappointing sponsors and the public, said Shoji Maruyama, chairman of the Japanese Ski Association's Alpine steering committee.
Saturday's forecast predicts rain and high winds in the morning, changing to snow during the day.

"For us, it's a special competition because its a pre-Olympic race," said race referee Kurt Hoch. "The skiers have travelled thousands of kilometres. I think considering it's a special situation that they should show more flexibility.
"I hope next year (during the Olympics) the Nagano organising committee is more flexible if we have problems with the weather," he added. "If not, maybe we won't have a race."
Maruyama said organisers risked losing sponsors for future World Cups if the schedule was changed. Also, more than 3,000 tickets had been sold for Saturday's race, mostly to out-of-town fans.
"Of course, we do understand the races are for racers," said Maruyama. "But for a big event like this there are also media and sponsors and the public, and you can't forget any of them.
"We can't be flexible in this situation," he added. "But for the Olympics next year we would like to try to be more flexible to prevent these kinds of situations."

Hoch also said that organisers refused to use chemical snow hardeners, which might be needed to save Friday's race since temperatures as high as nine degrees Celsius are expected before a cold front reaches Hakuba at dawn on Saturday.
Maruyama said organisers had begun packing the course in December, but never intended to use artificial snow hardeners.

Training was delayed for an hour on Thursday because of poor visibility caused by mild temperatures. Wednesday's training was cancelled because of heavy rains and wet snow, after skiers had their first training run on Tuesday.
World Cup overall leader Pernilla Wiberg clocked the fastest time, flashing down the 2,656-metre course in one minute, 37.57 seconds.
